title: Polio vaccine
what: The vaccine protects against polio, an infection that can cause paralysis. It is given as an injection or as drops in the mouth.
why: For children on the national vaccination schedule, and sometimes for adults before travel to high-risk countries.
duration: the vaccine itself takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If your child is sick now or has a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
If your child or someone in the family has weakened immunity. This matters for the drops

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when your child is healthy. Your child will be examined first.

prepare.title: Type of vaccine
prepare.text: Ask whether it will be a shot or drops. It depends on age and the schedule.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If drops are given, usually no feeding or drinks for about an hour afterward. Ask the nurse.

steps: The doctor examines your child and takes the temperature
If it is a shot, it is given in the thigh or arm
If it is drops, they are dropped into the mouth
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the vaccine, stay at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: A shot gives a quick pain; drops do not hurt
Sometimes redness at the shot spot or a mild fever
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
If your child spits up the drops right away, tell the nurse
red_flags: Trouble breathing, a swollen face, a rash all over: call your local emergency number
Weakness in a leg or arm after the vaccine: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: How is the shot different from the drops?
faq.a: The shot contains a killed virus; the drops contain a weakened live one. The doctor chooses the plan from the schedule.
Usually not, if the course was completed in childhood. Ask your doctor before travel to some countries.

reminders.text: Polio vaccine tomorrow. Bring the vaccination record.
